tagline.text: A limestone islet off Moalboal with sheer coral walls and top-tier diving

location.label: Location
location.text: Tañon Strait, off Panagsama Beach in Moalboal, western Cebu

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: December–May dry season (calmer seas and better visibility)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half a day (1–2 dives) to a full day

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱2,500–5,000 (per person, 1–2 dives or an island tour; based on booking-site examples)

children.text: Pescador Island is a small limestone island in the Tañon Strait off western Cebu, declared a marine park and fish sanctuary in 1990. Its sheer coral walls, sardine school and sea turtles make it the best-known dive site in Moalboal.

Pescador Island sits in the Tañon Strait off Moalboal on Cebu's west coast. It is a small limestone island that locals also call "Agad-Agad." The name Pescador is Spanish for "fisherman," said to come from the island's rich fishing grounds. Wikipedia gives the island's area as about 3.8 square kilometers, but in person it is tiny enough to take in at a glance from a boat, so figures may differ between sources. The island has a lighthouse and steps up on its north and east sides, and nobody lives there. Standing on the cliff at the southern end of Panagsama Beach in Moalboal, you can see the island across the water, and dive centers along the beach all market a trip here as their most popular product.

The island is famous for what lies underwater, not on land. The slope around it starts with sand and soft coral, then at about 5–10 m turns into a wall of hard coral that drops straight down to roughly 40 m. Because currents through the Tañon Strait bring in clear water, visibility is said to reach about 40 m on good days. Reports on dive-site listings range from about 18 to 30 m depending on the season and current, so treat conditions as different every day. On the west side there is an open-topped underwater cave nicknamed "The Cathedral," and it is described as a swim-through reached from the southern approach. Some trips cap groups at 4–5 divers per guide and require an Open Water certification plus at least 4 logged dives, so check before you book.

In 1990 the Sangguniang Bayan of Moalboal declared the island a marine park and fish sanctuary. Dive shops therefore pay a fee for every diver they bring, which is managed by the Moalboal municipal government and the Moalboal Dive Center Association and said to fund patrols against illegal fishing, garbage collection, environmental education, and coral and mangrove restoration. Sources quote different amounts, around
per dive, and the current figure could not be confirmed, so ask when booking whether it is included in your dive package.

Underwater, the sardine school is the signature sight. A large school of sardines has made this area its home; it is recorded that the school left after the February 2012 earthquake and larger predators declined, then returned in May 2013. When the sardines gather into a bait ball on the southern side, trevally, tuna and other predators may follow. Sea turtles are common, and reports also mention whitetip reef sharks resting on ledges, thresher sharks seen occasionally in deeper water, gorgonian fans, barrel sponges and black coral. These sightings come mostly from reviews, so nothing is guaranteed.
Starting from a sandy slope at 5–10 m, a hard-coral wall drops to about
. The standard way to see it is a drift dive along the wall. Currents and downcurrents are possible, so depth control matters.
Sardine schools move around the island, and when they ball up on the southern side, trevally and tuna gather to hunt. The school's position changes daily, so follow your guide to wherever it is.
This open-topped underwater cave on the west side is said to be a swim-through reached from the southern approach. Some dive products require an Open Water certification and at least 4 logged dives.
Reviews list sea turtles as common, and hawksbills feeding on sponges have been reported. The rule is simple: do not chase or touch them.

In the shallows around the island, even snorkelers are said to see turtles, sardines and tropical fish, and many island tours include it. Currents can be strong on the wall side on some days, so follow your guide's instructions.

The island has a lighthouse and steps on its north and east sides. A boat loop around it shows steep limestone walls with scrubby grass and trees. Whether you can land depends on the season and local rules, so ask your boat operator.
Since the 1990 designation, diver fees have paid for patrols, garbage collection and coral restoration. In effect, the fee you pay goes to the island's upkeep.

blocks.title: The island seen from Panagsama Beach

children.text: The island is visible across the water from the cliff at the southern end of Panagsama Beach. Even if you do not dive, it is a pleasant backdrop for a day at the beachfront resorts and restaurants.
Get fitted with gear and attend the briefing at a dive center on Panagsama. Bring your certification card and logbook.
Head out on the dive boat. Operators quote about
15–30 minutes
to reach the island.
Enter the water on the south side and drift along the wall. Stay within the depth limit set by your guide.
After a surface interval, do a second dive if you like, or return to Moalboal beach.
Sardines and turtles are said to be relatively calm early in the morning, but nothing is guaranteed.

items.title: Snorkeler's full day
items.subtitle: Island tour and the sardine school

children.text: Travel from your lodging to Panagsama and join the tour.
Take the boat to the waters around Pescador Island and snorkel.
Continue snorkeling at the sardine school or turtle spots near the shore.
Have lunch at a restaurant on Panagsama.
Relax on the beach, or connect to a trip to nearby Kawasan Falls.
Daily direct flights run from Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila to Mactan–Cebu International Airport (CEB), taking about
1 hour 30 minutes
. Check schedules with the airlines.
From the airport to the South Bus Terminal in Cebu City takes about
30 minutes–1 hour
by taxi or Grab.
Take a west-coast bus from the South Bus Terminal and get off in Moalboal. The ride is known to take about
3–4 hours
; routes and fares change, so confirm locally.
A taxi, rental car or airport pickup van is more comfortable but costs more. Negotiate the price before you book.

items.title: Boat from Moalboal to the island

children.text: The island is reached by boat from the dive centers on Panagsama Beach. It takes about
15–30 minutes
depending on the operator.
Book both regular outrigger boats and dive boats through local operators. Currents in the strait can be strong, and trips may be cancelled on rough days.
From Moalboal town to Panagsama Beach, take a tricycle or motorcycle taxi. Fares depend on distance and haggling, so confirm locally.

You can dive Pescador Island all year, but the dry season, when the sea is calm and visibility is good, suits it best. Reviewers reported visibility of about 30 m in July, about 18 m in November and about 25 m in March, with different currents each time.
Sardines and turtles are described as year-round sights, but their location changes daily. On days with strong currents the strait-side points get harder, so plan according to your skill level.

There is no lodging or restaurant on the island, so stay on Panagsama Beach or in Moalboal town and go out by boat. Panagsama is lined with dive centers, resorts and beachfront restaurants, which makes meals before and after diving easy. Prices and facilities change often, so check recent reviews on booking sites.

Restaurants along the beach serve seafood, Filipino home cooking and Western dishes. On the boat you usually need to bring your own water and snacks, so ask in advance whether they are included in your tour.

Diving here requires at least an Open Water certification and a logbook, and the site is rated for advanced divers because of currents and downcurrents. If you have limited experience, tell your guide honestly.
The wall and the sardine school can distract you, and it is easy to drift deeper. Always stay within your computer's and guide's limits.
Do not touch or stand on coral, and do not get too close to turtles or the sardine school. The marine park is kept going by diver fees.
When booking, compare whether the package price includes the marine park fee, gear rental and lunch.
Even if you only plan to snorkel, wear a life vest and stay with your guide. The strait is a place where currents change.
Leave early in the morning for lower waves and good light. Winds can pick up in the afternoon, so schedule earlier.
Bring a dry bag, reef-safe sunscreen and a spare towel. The boat has almost no shade.
Carry plenty of cash. Some beachfront shops do not accept cards or e-payments.
Currents and downcurrents in the Tañon Strait vary daily, so always follow your guide's briefing and depth limits.
On days with strong currents, entering on the strait side can be dangerous. If the guide cancels, accept it.
Fees and rules are set by the local government and the dive association and may change. Check the latest notices.
Use a dry bag so belongings do not fall into the water when boarding or disembarking.
Observe no-fly intervals after diving. A set gap is usually required before flying, so leave room in your schedule.

Landing on the island or approaching the lighthouse may be restricted at times. A report cited on Wikipedia says the island was closed to the public for about three months in January 2022, so check before you go.
The coastal town where boats to the island depart. Sardines and sea turtles are said to be found close to the beach.
An emerald-green waterfall reached by road from Moalboal; check travel time locally. Day trips combined with canyoneering are common.
A town at the southern tip of Cebu that you can combine with marine activities for a day or two more.
